mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals an easing monetary policy that reduces discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods where FEDFUNDS has declined for 3 consecutive months, or the Rank IC over 5-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) increase exceeding 0.3 percentage points signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered instances (UNRATE increase > 0.3pp), or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicate broad-based consumer demand contraction that triggers negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days as corporate revenue expectations decline.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods where both HOUST and RSAFS decline for 2 consecutive months, or the Rank IC over 5-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a manufacturing supply shock regime (annual INDPRO growth < 0.5%), a monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals deepening economic slowdown that reduces corporate profit visibility, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered instances (INDPRO decline in supply shock regime), or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A rising quarterly GDP growth rate (GDPC1) indicates expanding economic activity that supports corporate earnings growth, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods with rising GDPC1, or the Rank IC over 5-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Year-over-year CPI inflation (CPIAUCSL) exceeding 3.5% signals persistent inflation that may trigger aggressive monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered instances (CPIAUCSL YoY > 3.5%), or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) and rising unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicate labor market deterioration that reduces consumer spending and corporate profit outlook, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods where PAYEMS declines and UNRATE rises, or the Rank IC over 5-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening regime (FEDFUNDS > 4.5%), a monthly increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals aggressive policy that reduces liquidity and equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered instances (FEDFUNDS increase in tightening regime), or the Rank IC over 5-year rolling windows is below 0.03.
